cells.tense: The work is going deep right now and the passes are getting finer.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Take one distinction in this work — what's essential versus what only looks like it — and look at it closely. Keep the answer even if it's small. Sitting alone with it is part of the work.
cells.core:
You can tell the difference between what carries the work and what only looks like it should. That's what makes the long practice pay — each pass gets closer to what the thing actually needs, and that closeness is the skill. Time alone at the bench doesn't cut you off from anything. It's where the refining happens, and what you bring back is real.

Spend one sitting on a single distinction — the one that keeps coming up. Look close, decide which side of it matters, and don't try to settle the whole craft at once. Stay with the one you chose. That's the pass you're on, and it's enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: Each pass you make is getting closer to the thing itself.
cells.verb: deepening a craft past the point where it first worked
cells.place: where you become what you already are

cells.tense: You will have it finished and polished before the work has shown you what it needs.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, the day it happens
cells.ask: When something in this work goes well, tell someone who'd care that day, not later. Keep the telling small and true, then let the deeper pass wait until the work asks for it.
cells.core:
The finishing is racing past the making. You're polishing what isn't built yet, and the work keeps answering to a standard it can't reach, which reads from the outside as strain. The pace is set where the craft can't feed you.

A rough version can be worth showing, and often is. The making gets to set the pace, not the finish. Let one good thing be finished in the open. Mark it the day it happens with someone who'd want to know, and stay with the gladness while it's here. A version shared today is worth more than a perfect one you can't hand over.
cells.sheetLine: You're polishing a piece the work hasn't finished showing you.

cells.tense: The threshold you keep standing in front of was crossed a while back, and you haven't moved.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Say what this work is, once, to whoever's nearby — what it is, where it stands, what comes next. Plain. No argument after it.
cells.core:
At its best, this work gets stated as what it is. You name the shape once, plainly, and anyone listening can see what's been made. It's something you can hand over, not a claim to defend.

Lately the whole thing goes unclaimed. What you've built is standing there, and you talk as though it hadn't started. Say its shape plainly to whoever's nearby — one statement, then let it stand. Then go back to it. The structure has held for a while, and saying it out loud is how you keep standing in it.
cells.sheetLine: You've built the thing and keep talking as if you hadn't.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing, and you call it waiting.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Set the speed of this work by what you can actually keep, then hold it there for a stretch. If that's slower than you planned, slower is fine.
cells.core:
The direction of this practice comes from what you care about, and the effort is yours — the work continues because you continue it, and that counts as steering.

The practice keeps moving, and the account you'd give has the motion coming from elsewhere. The hands at the bench are yours, but the description leaves your hand out of it. What you feel about the work is what carries it, and that feeling hasn't been counted as direction.

Set a pace you can hold for a month, not a day, and stay with it. If it's slower than you planned, let it be slower and keep going. The momentum is yours, and it runs at your speed.
cells.sheetLine: The work moves because you do, at the speed you set.
